pages.title: Building a Turbine
pages.text: The smallest turbine is $(thing)5 x 4 x 5$(). The one on the next page is $(thing)5 x 5 x 5$(), which gives room for two blade layers and one coil layer.$(br2)Press the eye button to project it into the world.

pages.name: Basic Turbine
pages.text: Bearings top and bottom, a shaft between them, blades on the two lower layers and a ring of iron coils on the upper one.

pages.title: Blades and coils
pages.text: Every layer along the shaft is either blades or coils, never both, and all the blade layers have to sit together at one end.$(br2)More blade layers means more torque and a faster spin up. More coil layers means more power drawn per rotation. Which split you want depends on the flow rate you can feed it.

pages.title: Feeding it
pages.text: Set one Fluid Port to Inlet and the other to Outlet. Pipe steam from your reactor into the inlet, and the condensed water back to the reactor from the outlet.$(br2)Closing that loop means you never have to supply fresh water again.

pages.title: Tuning
pages.text: Start the turbine with the coils disengaged and let the rotor spin up. Watch the RPM climb, and engage the coils as it approaches $(thing)900$() or $(thing)1800$() RPM.$(br2)Then trim the flow rate until the RPM sits still at that number. That is the whole tuning process.
